title: Maximum Length of Semi-Decreasing Subarrays
statement:
Call a non-empty array **semi-decreasing** when its first element is strictly larger than its last element (the elements in between may be anything).

Given the integer array `nums`, return the length of its longest contiguous, non-empty subarray that is semi-decreasing. If no subarray qualifies, return `0`. A single element never qualifies, because its first and last elements are the same.
notes:
## Intuition

The brute force tries every left end and looks for the farthest smaller value to its right, which is O(n²). Notice that a left end `i` is pointless if some earlier index holds a value at least as large: that earlier index gives a longer subarray with a first element that is just as big. So the only useful left ends are the **strict prefix maxima**, values larger than everything before them. Their indices and values both increase, which makes them a monotonic stack.

## Approach

1. Scan left to right and push `left` onto `stack` whenever `nums[left]` beats the value at the top. The stack now holds the strict prefix maxima, largest on top.
2. Scan `right` from the end towards the start.
3. While the top's value is greater than `nums[right]`, this `right` is the farthest partner that top will ever get, so pop it and update `best` with `right - left + 1`.
4. If the top is not greater, no lower entry is either (their values are smaller), so move `right` on.
5. Return `best` (still `0` if nothing was popped with a real length).

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [7,6,5,4,3,2,1,6,10,11]`. The prefix maxima are indices `0, 8, 9` (values 7, 10, 11). At `right = 9` nothing pops. At `right = 8`, 11 > 10 pops index 9 with length 0. At `right = 7` (value 6), 10 > 6 pops index 8 (length 0) and 7 > 6 pops index 0 with length `7 - 0 + 1 = 8`. The stack is empty, so the answer is `8`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each index is pushed and popped at most once.
- Space: O(n) for the stack.

## Pitfalls

- The comparison is strict: equal first and last values do not count, and a single element is never an answer.
- An index popped after `right` has passed it gives a length of 0 or less; it never had a partner, and starting `best` at `0` ignores it.
- Do not stop at the first pair found; the longest one may start at an early prefix maximum.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `stack` | indices of strict prefix maxima, increasing in index and value |
| `left` | a candidate start index |
| `right` | the end index being tried, from the back |
| `best` | longest semi-decreasing length found |

narration.2: The stack will hold the only start indices worth trying.
narration.3: Walk the array from the left to collect candidate starts.
narration.4: Keep an index only if its value is larger than every value before it.
narration.5: Push it; earlier, larger-or-equal values would dominate any other index.
narration.10: Try end positions from the back, so each start meets its farthest partner first.
narration.11: The top start is larger than this end, so the pair is semi-decreasing.
narration.12: Pop it: any later end would be closer and give a shorter subarray.
narration.13: Record the length; an index already behind right gives a length of 0 or less and changes nothing.
narration.16: Return the longest length, or 0 if no pair qualified.
